Problem_Classification.Algorithm_Purpose: Computes the optimal global alignment score between two sequences by filling a 2D dynamic-programming score matrix. Each cell H[i,j] = max( H[i-1,j-1] + sub(i,j), H[i-1,j] - penalty, H[i,j-1] - penalty ), where sub(i,j) is the substitution score from BLOSUM62. The bottom-right cell holds the optimal alignment score; an optional traceback recovers the alignment path.
Problem_Classification.Algorithm_Steps: 1. Host initializes input_itemsets (the H matrix) with random values along row 0 and column 0, then overwrites them with gap-penalty initialization (-i*penalty / -j*penalty). 2. Host builds the reference (substitution) matrix by indexing BLOSUM62 with input_itemsets row/column headers. 3. Both arrays are copied to device memory (d_input_itemsets, d_reference). 4. Tiled wavefront sweep across the matrix using two diagonal phases: a. Upper-left phase (kernel1): for blk = 1..block_width, launch `blk` blocks of `BLOCK_SIZE` threads. Each block processes one 16×16 tile that lies on the anti-diagonal blk; tiles in the same wavefront are independent and run in parallel. b. Lower-right phase (kernel2): for blk = block_width-1..1, launch `blk` blocks; tiles cover the remaining anti-diagonals of the lower-right triangle. 5. Inside each kernel: thread 0 loads the NW corner from global memory; every thread loads one column (BLOCK_SIZE entries) of the reference tile and one entry of the N and W boundaries into shared memory; __syncthreads() barrier; an anti-diagonal sweep inside the tile (m = 0..BLOCK_SIZE-1, then m = BLOCK_SIZE-2..0) fills the (BLOCK_SIZE+1)×(BLOCK_SIZE+1) shared score tile with __syncthreads() between waves; finally each thread writes its column of the BLOCK_SIZE×BLOCK_SIZE result back to global memory. 6. After (warmup + repeat) iterations, the device result is copied back and compared against the CPU reference (nw_host); the traceback (when TRACEBACK is defined) reconstructs the alignment path from the final score matrix.
Problem_Classification.Reference_Complexity: Time: O(N · M) cell updates with sequential anti-diagonal dependency depth O(N + M); each cell is O(1). Space: O(N · M) for the H/score matrix and the reference (substitution) matrix. Shared-memory footprint per block is O(BLOCK_SIZE²).

Bottleneck_Analysis.Classification: Latency-bound (with secondary memory-bandwidth pressure); strictly NOT compute-bound
Bottleneck_Analysis.Arithmetic_Intensity: Per 16×16 tile, global-memory traffic: Reads = 256 (reference tile) + 1 (NW) + 16 (W column) + 16 (N row) = 289 int32 = 1156 B Writes = 256 int32 = 1024 B Total ≈ 2180 B per tile. Compute per tile ≈ 256 cells × ~5 integer ops (one add, two subtracts, two compares in `maximum`) ≈ 1280 int-ops. Arithmetic intensity ≈ 1280 / 2180 ≈ 0.59 int-ops / byte. (Counting only the FMA-equivalent "useful" max-plus-add as 2 ops yields ~0.23 ops/B — same order.)
Bottleneck_Analysis.Ridge_Point_Comparison: RTX A6000 INT32 peak ≈ 84 SM × 64 INT32-ops/cycle × ~1.80 GHz ≈ 9.7 TIOPS. Peak DRAM BW = 768 GB/s. Ridge point ≈ 9700 / 768 ≈ 12.6 ops/byte. Kernel AI (≈0.59 ops/B) is roughly 20× BELOW the ridge → strictly memory-bandwidth limited from a roofline standpoint.
Bottleneck_Analysis.Dominant_Limiter: In practice the kernel is dominated by KERNEL-LAUNCH LATENCY and OCCUPANCY STARVATION rather than raw DRAM bandwidth: • 2·(block_width − 1) + 1 kernel launches per outer iteration; each launch has only `blk` blocks of 16 threads (½ warp). For a typical 2048-element problem (block_width=128), most launches contain far fewer blocks than the 84 SMs available, especially at the start/end of each phase. • Every block uses just 16 threads = 1 half-warp, so SIMT lanes are 50% wasted before any other inefficiency. • The anti-diagonal wavefront imposes a serial chain of ~2·block_width kernel launches, each with __syncthreads() inside, so the critical path is launch + sync latency, not bandwidth. Secondary limiter: uncoalesced/strided global stores (each thread writes BLOCK_SIZE rows separated by `max_cols`, see Memory_Access_Profile).

Memory_Access_Profile.Pattern: Tiled sliding-window over a 2D matrix with anti-diagonal wavefront dependency; per-thread access to global memory is column-strided (stride = max_cols * sizeof(int)) for both the reference load and the output store, with short coalesced loads along the N boundary.
Memory_Access_Profile.Read_Write_Ratio: Per tile: 289 reads vs 256 writes ≈ 1.13 : 1 (essentially balanced ~9:8). Including the host→device copy of both buffers once and the final D→H copy of one buffer, overall read:write to DRAM across the program ≈ 1.1 : 1.
Memory_Access_Profile.Reuse_Factor: Reference tile entries: 1× (loaded once into shared memory, read multiple times during the in-tile wavefront; ~2 logical re-reads per cell after the initial load). Score tile entries: each interior cell is read 3× (by its E, S, SE neighbors) and written 1× — all served from shared memory after initial boundary load. Net global-memory reuse factor ≈ 1× (no inter-tile reuse of H in this implementation; the NW/N/W boundaries are re-fetched by neighboring tiles).
Memory_Access_Profile.Coalescing_Feasibility: Requires transformation. As written: • The reference load `d_reference[index + max_cols * ty]` has 32 threads each reading one column → already coalesced within a warp for the `tx` dimension, GOOD. • The W-boundary load `d_input_itemsets[index_w + max_cols * tx]` is column-strided across threads → UNCOALESCED (stride = max_cols ints). • The final write loop `d_input_itemsets[index + max_cols * ty]` writes one column per thread → 16 consecutive int writes per warp per ty, COALESCED within the warp but only 16 lanes active. Fully coalescing the W load would require a transpose or rearrangement of the H buffer (or staging through shared memory differently).
Memory_Access_Profile.Optimal_Tiling_Hint: Current tile = 16×16 with shared-memory cost ≈ 17·17·4 + 16·16·4 = 1156 + 1024 = 2180 B/block. Plenty of headroom. Recommended: increase tile to 32×32 (uses ~33·33·4 + 32·32·4 = 8.45 KB/block, still trivially fits in 100 KB/SM), launch 32 threads/block = full warp (eliminates the 50% lane waste), and fuse the two phases or use a single persistent-block scheme with global atomics-free dependency tracking to amortize launch latency. For very large problems, consider a diagonal-major layout (skew transform) so that an entire anti-diagonal becomes a contiguous 1-D array and global accesses are fully coalesced.

Parallelism_Structure.Granularity: One CUDA thread = one column of a 16×16 tile (16 cells, processed serially along the in-tile wavefront). One CUDA block = one 16×16 tile of the H matrix.
Parallelism_Structure.Independence: Has RAW dependency. Inter-tile: each tile depends on its N, W, and NW neighbor tiles (anti-diagonal wavefront). Intra-tile: each cell depends on its N, W, NW cells, serialized by the m-loop with __syncthreads() between waves. Tiles on the same anti-diagonal are fully independent and form the only source of parallelism.
Parallelism_Structure.Synchronization: Intra-block: __syncthreads() — once after shared-memory loads, then once per anti-diagonal step (2·BLOCK_SIZE − 1 barriers per tile). Inter-block: implicit via kernel-boundary synchronization (the host serializes anti-diagonals by launching one kernel per wavefront). No atomics, no cooperative groups.
Parallelism_Structure.Recommended_Block_Size: Current 16 threads/block is sub-optimal on SM_86 (1 half-warp, 50% lane utilization, max 48 blocks/SM = 768 threads/SM out of 1536, ≤50% occupancy ceiling from threads alone, before shared-memory/register limits). Theoretical recommendation: 32 threads/block (one warp, paired with a 32×32 tile) or 64 threads/block, which keep one warp/block fully active and approach full 1536 threads/SM occupancy on SM_86 while still fitting in shared memory and registers.

Hardware_Constraints.Shared_Memory_Per_Block: 48 KB default, up to 99 KB opt-in (cudaFuncSetAttribute)
Hardware_Constraints.Shared_Memory_Per_SM: 100 KB (configurable: 100 KB shared / 28 KB L1 split on SM_86)
Hardware_Constraints.GPU_Clock_Rate: Boost up to 2100 MHz (per nvidia-smi); typical sustained ~1.80 GHz

Data_Shape.Input_Dimensions: Square H matrix of size max_rows × max_cols, where max_rows = max_cols = atoi(argv[1]) + 1. argv[1] is constrained to a multiple of 16. Typical benchmark sizes are 1024, 2048, 4096, or 8192. Reference matrix is the same shape. The wavefront block grid is block_width × block_width where block_width = argv[1] / 16.
Data_Shape.Data_Type: int32 (signed `int`) for input_itemsets, reference, output_itemsets, and BLOSUM62 substitution scores.
Data_Shape.Total_Memory_Footprint: Per buffer: max_rows · max_cols · 4 B. Device-side: 2 buffers → 2 · (N+1)² · 4 B. Host-side: 3 buffers (input, reference, output) → 3 · (N+1)² · 4 B. Worked examples (N = argv[1]): N = 1024 → device ≈ 8.4 MB, host ≈ 12.6 MB N = 2048 → device ≈ 33.6 MB, host ≈ 50.4 MB N = 4096 → device ≈ 134 MB, host ≈ 201 MB N = 8192 → device ≈ 537 MB, host ≈ 805 MB All sizes are comfortably below the 48 GB VRAM (and the 9.96 GB currently free reported by nvidia-smi) for any reasonable bioinformatics problem; the L2 cache (6 MB) can hold the working set only for N ≲ 880.
